The '''Royal Scriptorial Decree''' was an early standardization of the [[Vesperan Alphabet]], dated by source material to around 1350 and associated with [[King Aurelius III]].

== Significance ==

The decree represents the point where Vesperan writing began to move from local scribal practice toward a more formal royal and religious standard. Source material says it expanded the older western letter inventory, regularized letter forms, and supported the use of written Vesperan in royal and sacred documents.

== Legacy ==

Later Vesperan states treated the decree as a predecessor to the [[Royal Language Decree of 1652]] and the imperial reforms of the eighteenth century. It gave later Vesperan scholars a foundation story for the script's antiquity and independence.

== Canon Note ==

The surrounding political world of the fourteenth-century western kingdoms is not yet fully drafted. This page preserves the date and script role without making map-level claims about borders or dynasties beyond the source's connection to King Aurelius III.
